nodes.label: First Vertical Slice Scenario
nodes.rationale: A convincing DDD/CQRS/ES showcase must demonstrate more than folders: a reviewer should be able to repeat a request, stop workers, redeliver work, corrupt derived state and rebuild it without creating contradictory business history.

nodes.label: T5 — Payments Domain, Events and Schema
nodes.norm_label: t5 — payments domain, events and schema

nodes.label: PaymentInitiated Event Contract
nodes.rationale: Stable identity is the alias payments.payment_initiated, not the class name, so the namespace can move without rewriting history. Schema version 1 comes from an overridden eventVersion() rather than Spatie's attribute, because ADR 0002 permits exactly two vendor types in Domain.

nodes.label: occurredAt as a String
nodes.rationale: Symfony's DateTimeNormalizer in Spatie's default chain formats with RFC3339, which has no sub-second component, so a DateTimeImmutable property would silently truncate business time to whole seconds in the stored payload. The canonical format is Y-m-d\TH:i:s.uP at +00:00, validated by a round-trip that also rejects overflowing dates.

nodes.label: Payments Projection Gate
nodes.rationale: payment_projection_controls is durable operator-visible ready/rebuilding state while advisory locks own mutual exclusion. Gate acquisition must be the first statement inside relayOne() and inside the consumer transaction, on the same injected connection, because the shared lock and the row lock it protects must report the same backend pid.

nodes.label: Gated Rebuild Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Rebuilding automatically after every discrepancy can destroy evidence, expose partial data or repeat external side effects, so repair and rebuild are explicit operator actions. Lock timeout aborts before clearing data, a killed run leaves the durable row as rebuilding, and ready is exposed only after complete success.

nodes.label: HS-1 — Deliberately Omitted Projection Gate
nodes.rationale: The relay acquires, simulates and stubs nothing of the projection gate because payment_projection_controls, its advisory-key derivation and its deferral semantics are T11's design. A provisional gate would either become permanent scope creep or be discarded, coupling two milestones for no present benefit. Absence is recorded as temporary scope, never as a permanent 'zero advisory locks' contract.

nodes.label: Lightweight ADR Format
nodes.rationale: ADRs exist for durable decisions implementation should not silently reverse. Each carries title/ID, status, date and owner, context, decision, rejected alternatives, consequences, and relations. Sequential filenames without dates keep ordering stable and references unbreakable.

nodes.label: Deferred Resumable Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Resumable checkpoints and a staging-table swap are required only once measured event volume, rebuild duration or restart cost violates an availability target; that future design must cover staging lifecycle, events arriving during replay, final catch-up, atomic swap, cleanup and crash recovery at every transition.

nodes.label: Evolution-trigger discipline (do not build in anticipation of load)
nodes.norm_label: evolution-trigger discipline (do not build in anticipation of load)

nodes.label: External Trackers (Linear and Asana)
nodes.rationale: Linear and Asana intentionally mirror M1–M5 during a tool comparison; neither tracker is the architecture source of truth. Tracker descriptions link to document paths and may not link tasks to each other across products.

nodes.label: M5 — Verification, Rebuild, and Resilience Proof
nodes.norm_label: m5 — verification, rebuild, and resilience proof

nodes.label: T13 — Resilience Demo and Operational Guide
nodes.norm_label: t13 — resilience demo and operational guide

nodes.label: Resilience Evidence Ownership Split
nodes.rationale: T8 owns duplicate-delivery, marker-repair, poison-exhaustion and operator-retry evidence through a deterministic failpoint plus a live Horizon stop/backlog/restart smoke; T9 owns the projected, pending, missing, malformed and foreign-ownership query bullets; the barrier-coordinated SIGTERM/SIGKILL multi-process suite and the gate-dependent bullets stay with T12 and T11.

nodes.label: Documentation Ownership Rules
nodes.rationale: Each document should answer one class of question instead of accumulating unrelated implementation detail: architecture explains boundaries and trade-offs, specifications define behavior and invariants, the roadmap owns delivery order, testing maps behavior to evidence, operations owns process topology, and ADRs record durable decisions. Pointers are preferred over copied narrative so a behavior change is edited in exactly one canonical place.

nodes.label: Sequential Delivery Order
nodes.rationale: Implementation is intentionally sequential across schema and state-machine tasks. Review and test-writing agents may inspect a completed milestone in parallel, but concurrent worktrees must not modify the same Payments persistence contracts. A failed compatibility invariant blocks dependent feature work instead of hiding behind later tasks.

nodes.label: Tracked Graph Artifacts Policy
nodes.rationale: Exactly four graphify-out artifacts are tracked because they are the queryable graph, marked linguist-generated with -diff -merge so a conflict is resolved by regenerating rather than hand-editing. Everything machine-local (cache, manifest, absolute host paths, signatures) is ignored, and the graph refresh is committed after the source commit it analyzes so its build stamp names a commit containing the analyzed source.

nodes.label: RelayPaymentOutboxCommand
nodes.rationale: The 750 ms budget is a start budget checked before each next row, never a kill deadline, so a row already begun always finishes committing or rolling back.

nodes.label: T4 Blocking Compatibility Evidence (Q6–Q10)
nodes.rationale: Advisory-lock affinity, shared/exclusive contention, a real 55P03 from a bounded lock_timeout, publication visible in Redis before the commit and a crash producing a safe duplicate were all measured. No worker consumed a message, SKIP LOCKED and multi-process behavior were untouched, and the advisory key is a spike constant — the production derivation belongs to T11.

nodes.label: payment_outbox Envelope and Active Index
nodes.rationale: The unique (aggregate_uuid, aggregate_version) mirrors the key stored_events already enforces, making a duplicate envelope impossible rather than merely detectable by the verifier. Payments-authored keys are named explicitly because PostgreSQL truncates identifiers at 63 bytes and a truncated name cannot be dropped by a later migration's computed name.

nodes.label: Deterministic Consumer Transaction
nodes.rationale: The transaction deliberately opens on the envelope row lock, not on a gate, because the control table and its advisory-key derivation are T11's design. Projection has one application attempt and does not reuse initiation's RetryingAtomicTransaction: a serialization retry loop belongs to the write path that owns its own idempotency receipt, while here redelivery and outbox reconciliation own recovery.

nodes.label: Durable Projection Schema
nodes.rationale: payment_projector_receipts carries no foreign key to payment_outbox or stored_events because the outbox is rebuildable delivery state, stored_events is vendor-owned, and the receipt must outlive both. payment_details has no mutable updated_at, so a duplicate delivery has nothing legitimate to touch. No secondary index is added without measured query-plan evidence.

nodes.label: payments:outbox:repair
nodes.rationale: Explicit and audited: it reconstructs only the derived envelope from the canonical stored event, refuses an orphan envelope without a canonical event, and can never create or change an idempotency receipt. Bulk repair is separate reviewed scope.

nodes.label: Ambiguous Commit Outcome
nodes.rationale: A failure firing after getPdo()->commit() succeeds is classified commit_outcome_unknown, aborts non-zero and does not republish in the same pass; the next pass reads canonical row state. Laravel can retain stale transaction bookkeeping after connection loss, so the relay never guesses whether the work rolled back.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED Relay Concurrency
nodes.rationale: Scheduler uniqueness (withoutOverlapping()/onOneServer()) was deliberately not registered: SKIP LOCKED already makes overlapping relay passes safe, so a scheduler-level mutex would be a second redundant owner of the same guarantee. Its absence is asserted by a runtime-contract test rather than left implicit.

nodes.label: Evolution Gate — Claim/Lease Publishing
nodes.rationale: Lock-through-push is intentionally simple. A claim/lease redesign is triggered only by sustained measurement: pool saturation or >20% API p95 regression attributable to relay-held connections, oldest eligible age above five seconds for five continuous minutes on a healthy transport, or safe concurrency failing throughput after tuning. A transient outage alone is not a trigger.

nodes.label: Completion-Marker Self-Healing
nodes.rationale: A duplicate leaves PaymentDetails unchanged and fills only a missing completion marker; the UPDATE carries 'and projection_completed_at is null' so its affected-row count is the outcome. A receipt whose read row is missing is corruption for verification and rebuild, not an excuse to silently recreate state, and a contradictory identity must fail visibly rather than be hidden by an upsert.

nodes.label: Session-Loss Inference Hazard
nodes.rationale: Outside a transaction Laravel reconnects silently onto a new backend, and inside one the loss surfaces while transactionLevel() still reports 1 because reconnect() swaps only the PDO. Therefore neither a successful query nor a non-zero transaction level is evidence that the pinned session or its advisory lock survived; the abort path needs a positive check — a re-read control row on a known-live connection, a fenced token, or a refusal to reconnect.

nodes.label: Failure Injection Policy
nodes.rationale: Failures are injected at named persistence and delivery checkpoints; process tests use synchronization barriers before SIGTERM/SIGKILL and arbitrary sleeps are not accepted as coordination. Production logic contains no environment-conditioned fault flags.

nodes.label: Query a Payment Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Unknown and foreign payment ids are byte-identical for one requested id so the endpoint never reveals that a payment exists but belongs to someone else; a malformed id shares the problem type and code and differs only in the instance path it echoes, and is never downgraded to the generic not_found.

nodes.label: M4 — Relay, Projection, and Query
nodes.rationale: M4's POST -> outbox -> Redis -> consumer -> GET exit is composed from T6, T7, T8 and T9 evidence rather than one measured end-to-end run; the full-chain resilience matrix stays T12's.

nodes.label: Merchant-Scoped Idempotency Receipt
nodes.rationale: Raw idempotency keys are hashed for lookup and never enter events, outbox payloads or logs; hashing gives fixed-width lookup and reduces casual plaintext exposure, but it is not encryption.

nodes.label: DatabasePaymentQuery Adapter
nodes.rationale: Both lookups run in one short adapter-owned transaction on one injected connection object, which is exactly what T11 relies on when it prepends a connection-affine gate to the same transaction. The adapter may read only payment_details and payment_idempotency_receipts, writes nothing, never rehydrates PaymentAggregate, and refuses a malformed id before PostgreSQL sees an invalid UUID.

nodes.label: GET /api/payments/{paymentId} Contract
nodes.rationale: 202 projection_pending is read-model transport state, not a domain payment status, and nothing durable records it; the body carries no completion estimate and no queue or worker state. 503 projection_rebuilding is unreachable until T11 ships, so T9 adds neither the problem code nor a provisional control table — an enum case with no producer is a promise nothing keeps.

nodes.label: Payments Architecture Test Rules
nodes.rationale: Payments Domain cannot depend on Laravel, Eloquent, HTTP, Redis, SQS or queue types; only ADR-listed Spatie base types are allowed; raw concurrency SQL stays inside its focused Infrastructure owner; and queries never rehydrate PaymentAggregate.

nodes.label: Eight Production Types Budget
nodes.rationale: RelayConfiguration, TransportBackoff, ProjectPaymentEvent, RelayOutcome, OutboxRelay, RelayHeartbeat, RelayPaymentOutboxCommand, PaymentOutboxStatusCommand and no ninth: no generic transport abstraction and no custom consumer exception were added ahead of a second implementation that would need them.

nodes.label: No Dependency Without a Consumer
nodes.rationale: No dependency is added because it is fashionable and none is kept without a consumer: laravel/pail was removed, install:api was not run, and spatie/laravel-data is deferred until a DTO needs casting, transformation or more than one representation. T6 shipped three DTO-shaped types and installed nothing.

nodes.label: RFC 9457 Problem Details Contract
nodes.rationale: Mapping is by exception type first and status only as fallback, because prepareJsonResponse() gives any non-HttpException a 500 before the hook runs and Application-layer exceptions cannot implement HttpExceptionInterface without breaking the module boundary — a status-driven mapper would ship the 409 as a 500. detail is a fixed client-safe sentence per code, never an exception message, which routinely carries SQL and table names.

nodes.label: ADR Candidate Backlog
nodes.rationale: An ADR is written when its implementation milestone begins, so measured package behavior and evidence can inform the final record rather than being guessed in advance.

nodes.label: Redis/SQS Capability Map
nodes.rationale: Redis cache, Redis locks, Redis Pub/Sub, Redis queues and Amazon SQS each carry distinct delivery semantics, durable authority and supervision. Similar infrastructure names must not collapse those differences: Pub/Sub is fan-out, not durable queue storage.

nodes.label: Source-of-Truth Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: stored_events and idempotency receipts are not rebuildable; outbox, projector receipts and payment_details are derived. A Redis or SQS message is a transient delivery attempt never treated as truth.

nodes.label: OpenSearch Adoption Gate
nodes.rationale: OpenSearch is not provisioned for portfolio completeness; adoption requires a query PostgreSQL cannot serve, specified indexing/replay/consistency ownership, a justified cost, and understood security/backup/deletion requirements. Until then PostgreSQL projections are the default search source.

nodes.label: One Image, Independently Supervised Processes
nodes.rationale: The API image may run HTTP/Filament, Horizon, scheduler/relay, Reverb and future SQS workers; reusing an image does not merge their scaling, health, or restart ownership.

nodes.label: SQS Adoption Boundary
nodes.rationale: SQS/DLQ is adopted only for a distinct workload that benefits from AWS-native durability, visibility timeouts, redrive and independently scalable workers, and the first concrete workload must be selected and specified before implementation. Horizon does not supervise SQS.

nodes.label: One Job, One Transport Rule
nodes.rationale: One logical job has one selected transport in one environment; the same job is never dual-published to Redis and SQS to demonstrate both technologies. A legitimate fan-out requires two explicitly named integration messages with their own owners, idempotency contracts and failure policies.

nodes.label: Payments-Specific Transactional Outbox Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over direct event-store catch-up because it makes the database-to-broker failure window observable and recoverable, demonstrates relay crash recovery and idempotent consumption, and keeps the durable envelope independent of Redis. Trade-offs: more schema, retry state, tooling and tests; the relay holds a row lock through a bounded network push; deliberately Payments-specific with no shared bus justified by one use case.

nodes.label: Application Process Topology
nodes.rationale: Processes reuse the ledgerflow-api image where practical but stay independently supervised, scaled, restarted and observed, so each one carries its own failure evidence rather than hiding behind a shared container.

nodes.label: Repository Deploy Ownership
nodes.rationale: Application repositories build immutable images identified by commit SHA/digest; ledgerflow-infra consumes those artifacts rather than building application source, so deployment topology never leaks into application repositories.

nodes.label: Container Contract
nodes.rationale: The entrypoint ends in exec "$@" with CMD ["php-fpm"], so Horizon, the scheduler/relay, Reverb and future SQS workers reuse the same image with only a command: override — which is what makes image reuse true rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: Disposable-Project Image Build Limitation
nodes.rationale: docker/dockerfile:1 frontend resolution timed out over the session's registry proxy, so the disposable-project run retagged an already-built dev image. Recorded rather than smoothed over: it is not a fresh-build proof of the current Dockerfile, though the image content was proved current by the same make check.

nodes.label: Queue Transport Policy
nodes.rationale: Redis is chosen for M1–M5 so the relay, duplicates, Horizon supervision, failed jobs and local recovery are easy to observe, while PostgreSQL outbox state and projector receipts remain authoritative for recovery. The projection job and envelope must not depend on Redis types.

nodes.label: Scheduler Contract
nodes.rationale: The command is registered in root routes/console.php because ModuleBoundaryTest forbids a module carrying a routes directory — the same reason config/payments.php lives at the root. The healthcheck is payments:outbox:status rather than mere process existence, so a wedged loop or a lost database both fail it.

nodes.label: Bounded projection-contract Deadline
nodes.rationale: The 180-second deadline bounds the contract's work, not the whole wall clock, because guaranteed scoped cleanup takes precedence over a flat cap: teardown adds a separately bounded tail of at most four 10-second diagnostics plus one 60-second down --volumes. PROJECTION_CONTRACT_DEADLINE_SECONDS may shorten but never lengthen it.

nodes.label: Paired Scheduler+Horizon Activation
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no target that starts one process without the other: the relay publishes into payments-projection and Horizon is the only thing that drains it, so a scheduler running alone produces a growing backlog that reads as a consumer fault rather than as a missing process. projection-start depends on db-migrate so workers never start against a schema without payment_projector_receipts and payment_details.

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Job Permissions and Non-Persisted Credentials
nodes.norm_label: least-privilege job permissions and non-persisted credentials

nodes.label: Workflows Must Not Duplicate Tool Command Sequences
nodes.norm_label: workflows must not duplicate tool command sequences

nodes.label: GitHub Actions OIDC Role Assumption
nodes.rationale: Bounded AWS roles assumed via OIDC so no long-lived AWS keys are committed or stored as ordinary repository secrets.

nodes.label: User Interface Surface Ownership
nodes.rationale: ledgerflow-spa never reads the database, Redis, queues, or AWS services directly; it consumes stable API contracts and authorized realtime events.

nodes.label: Three-Repository Ownership Split
nodes.rationale: Application repos build immutable artifacts tagged by commit SHA; ledgerflow-infra consumes them rather than cloning and building application source, so infrastructure deployment never rebuilds application code.

nodes.label: Queue Failure Ownership
nodes.rationale: No queue is disposable merely because work can be replayed; every logical queue defines lag, failure, retry, poison and recovery evidence. Filament and the merchant dashboard never expose raw queue or DLQ controls.

nodes.label: Required Operational Evidence
nodes.rationale: Structured logs exclude raw idempotency keys and include payment, merchant, event, message and correlation identifiers. The verifier reports corruption and never repairs or rebuilds automatically; repair stays an explicit operator procedure with audit evidence.

nodes.label: Outbox State Transitions
nodes.rationale: An arbitrarily long transport outage never sets exhausted_at; only a confirmed consumer-handler exception increments the poison count, with five as the initial threshold. Worker termination, backlog and a missing receipt are not poison evidence. Initial timings are operational defaults, not domain rules.

nodes.label: payments:outbox:retry
nodes.rationale: The sole reactivation path for an exhausted envelope, working under a row lock and refusing without mutation when the event is unknown, completed or not exhausted. Setting available_at = now() is the one narrow exception to the relay's ownership of that column, so a corrected row becomes immediately eligible instead of waiting for a transport schedule it never earned.

nodes.label: Outbox Writer Ownership Split
nodes.rationale: T6 inserts the envelope, T7 mutates transport state only and never writes exhausted_at, T8 records consumer outcome and owns exhaustion. Splitting the failure increment from the threshold check across two owners would make the decision race — the count could reach five in one owner while the other evaluated a stale value. One writer, one transaction, no race.

nodes.label: Projection Failure Classification
nodes.rationale: Only a confirmed deterministic handler failure consumes the projection budget; backlog, transport failure, connection loss, commit uncertainty, lock/serialization/statement-timeout errors and gate deferral never count. Database failures are classified by SQLSTATE class and owned constraint identity, never by matching exception messages, so a driver wording change cannot silently move a failure between budgets.

nodes.label: projection_failure_generation Fence
nodes.rationale: A monotonic non-negative fence that only a successful operator retry increments lets a late failure recorder tell a delayed delivery apart from a new retry cycle. The recorder applies metadata only while the row is still incomplete, non-exhausted and on the generation captured under the projection transaction's lock, so there is no check-then-write window and a late recorder can poison neither a winning duplicate nor a reset cycle.

nodes.label: Payments Tracer Bullet
nodes.rationale: Normal path and rebuild path reuse the same deterministic projection application service, and rebuild never republishes integration side effects.

nodes.label: T3 Blocking Compatibility Evidence (Q1–Q5)
nodes.rationale: Only 55P03 was raised against a real database; 40P01 and 40001 remain allowlisted but unmeasured, and a genuine deadlock needs two concurrent processes, which belongs to the resilience plan. The spike harness is not parallel-safe because it commits real rows to a shared database.

nodes.label: Lock-Through-Push Publication
nodes.rationale: One row, one short PostgreSQL transaction, publish before commit, no shared gate. Claim/lease publishing was rejected as strictly more complex with no benefit until a measured failure attributes real cost to holding the connection across the Redis round trip; pushRaw() was rejected because it skips Queue::enqueueUsing() and cannot express the after-commit contract; a generic transport abstraction was rejected as an interface with one implementation.

nodes.label: Safe Duplicate Over Lost Message
nodes.rationale: Publishing inside the open transaction with after_commit => false means a crash between push and commit produces a duplicate rather than a lost message. An accepted-then-thrown Redis reply reaches the same ceiling by a different route: it commits durable rejection state and republishes after backoff. Both can only over-deliver, which consumer idempotency absorbs; neither can under-deliver.

nodes.label: Atomic Idempotent Write
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL owns durable idempotency because rate limiting cannot prove that retries create one business operation and a process may crash between reservation, event persistence and publication. The ON CONFLICT target is named rather than omitted: the table also carries a global unique on payment_id, and an untargeted clause would swallow that collision too, turning a permanent condition into a retryable 503.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE Retry Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Only 40P01, 40001 and 55P03 retry the closure, at most three times, and classification is owned here rather than delegated: Laravel's ConcurrencyErrorDetector matches 40P01 only through an English message and does not recognise 55P03 at all. SQLSTATE is read from errorInfo[0] with getCode() as fallback, DeadlockException unwrapped first, compared as a string.

nodes.label: False-Positive Publication Acknowledgement
nodes.rationale: phpredis returns false rather than throwing for ERR/NOSCRIPT/WRONGTYPE and RedisQueue::pushRaw() discards eval()'s return value, so such a reply is invisible to the relay and the acceptance path runs for a message never enqueued. The consequence is delayed retry, not message loss: the row becomes eligible again when the reconciliation grace lapses with no projection_completed_at. It is not repairable without abandoning push() for pushRaw(), which would break the after_commit contract the whole ordering depends on.

nodes.label: Transport Exception Classification
nodes.rationale: RedisException is the complete transport surface of the resolved push path, not a first approximation: every raisable type was derived from installed source and the four that cannot occur were ruled out rather than assumed. RedisClusterException extends RuntimeException, not RedisException, so introducing a cluster connection would be a breaking change to this classification rather than a configuration detail.

nodes.label: payments:projections:verify
nodes.rationale: Verification is read-only and distinguishes in-flight work from confirmed inconsistency, because the application cannot infer corruption from elapsed time alone — a missing projection may still be valid queue lag. It never mutates data or starts a rebuild automatically.

nodes.label: Scheduled projection verification and corruption alerting
nodes.norm_label: scheduled projection verification and corruption alerting

nodes.label: MerchantContext Tenant Resolution
nodes.rationale: A merchant identifier supplied by a client is never sufficient authority; ownership is resolved server-side from the authenticated user.

nodes.label: Frontend Deployment Gate
nodes.rationale: SSR/runtime hosting on ECR+Fargate versus a static S3/CloudFront build must be chosen from authentication, realtime, caching and product needs before implementation; the choice belongs to the SPA and infra repos, not backend code.

nodes.label: Deferred Sanctum/SPA Session Decisions
nodes.rationale: T6 deliberately decided nothing above the token: abilities unscoped, expiration null, cookie-versus-token mode, CORS, CSRF and deployment domains open. A server-to-server bearer test is evidence the guard works, not a selection of the SPA session mode; these move to Merchant dashboard integration.

nodes.label: Five-State Relay Heartbeat
nodes.rationale: The heartbeat is written in application UTC after a fully handled pass, not from PostgreSQL now(), because it records that a process made progress — a database outage must not be able to fake a scheduler outage. redis-data persisting across restarts means a restarted scheduler reports its previous run's heartbeat as stale, never falsely fresh.

nodes.label: schedule:work First-Tick Latency
nodes.rationale: ScheduleWorkCommand::work() spawns a fresh schedule:run subprocess only at second === 0 of each minute, so a freshly started container can wait ~60 real seconds for its first tick. start_period: 75s was measured against a ~62-second worst case rather than tuned by guess.

nodes.label: ADR 0002 Payments Domain Event-Sourcing Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Payments Domain may reference exactly two external Spatie classes matched as exact names in that module only; Projector is named and excluded because it writes a read model and belongs in Infrastructure. Widening the allowlist would grant Domain a type it must never reference.

nodes.label: Public Makefile Interface
nodes.rationale: All validation runs through public Make targets and CI calls the same ones, so local and CI behavior cannot drift into two implementations. Docker plus a small Makefile define the development contract; an editor does not.

nodes.label: PHPStan Level 10 Without Baseline
nodes.rationale: phpstan.neon forbids a baseline in writing, so a future slice that cannot hold level 10 must lower the level explicitly with a recorded reason instead of silently accumulating ignored errors. The prediction that the Payments slice would force a lowering did not come true.

nodes.label: Resilience Test Environment Rules
nodes.rationale: SQLite is not a substitute for PostgreSQL concurrency and advisory-lock behavior, and queue/database fakes are used only when the faked boundary is not the behavior under test. The plan does not invent commands before the scaffold that owns them exists.

nodes.label: Filament Admin Boundary
nodes.rationale: Filament serves business workflows only; it must not generically mutate stored events, projections, outbox rows, payment status, queue state or AWS resources. A business action calls the same Application command and domain invariants as an API action.

nodes.label: Reverb WebSocket Boundary
nodes.rationale: Redis Pub/Sub is transient fan-out, not a durable queue, and cannot be the authority for a payment transition; the browser recovers missed state through an API read after reconnecting.

nodes.label: $_SERVER Env-Precedence Defect
nodes.rationale: The trap let the suite reach the development database and also defeated the queue, cache and session declarations. tests/bootstrap.php now validates the declared values; the three transport declarations carry live assertions, while the database half of the fix still has no test of its own.

nodes.label: Known Deferred Concerns
nodes.rationale: Recorded so they are not rediscovered as surprises: public/storage is unserved, Pest suites are not statically analysed, .env edits require make start, make test leaves services running, and CI deliberately has no Docker layer caching.
